steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Ouch!

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: The hell's wrong with you, Theo? You have eyes, use them!

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: S-Sorry, Mr. Rory, I was just hoping to try my luck over at Lagran Street, see if I could get some potatoes—

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: Get lost!

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Sorry...

steps.name: Coachman's Voice
steps.text: Look out! The burdenbeast's panicking! Out of the way!

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: Stupid coachman! You nearly ran me over! Get back here!

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: That dung-for-brains ran off, just like that?!

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Mr. Rory, I...

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: Hah, look who DID get run over! Serves you right.

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: You're not going anywhere now! Let's go see the Dublinn folks. Maybe they'll give me potatoes for handing over a traitor—

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: Better stick to the back streets. Can't have someone else taking my spy...
The man grabs the boy's collar and drags him into a small, empty alley. The boy groans in anguish.

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: Weird. Did I forget the way?

steps.name: Voices in the Distance
steps.text: Gimme back my potatoes! Go and buy your own! They still have some at the shop!

steps.name: Voices in the Distance
steps.text: Give them back!

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: They still have potatoes?!
The man glances towards the voices, then at the broken body of the boy whose arm he is still grabbing.

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: He's dying. Would the Dublinners even give me anything for a dying kid? Could they even get anything out of him?

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: ...It's your lucky day, traitor.
The man shakes off the boy's hand, which had been grabbing his sleeve, and walks off briskly towards the voices.

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: My leg... it hurts...

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: I can't stand...

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Mrs. Emma...

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Wh-Who's there? Who's calling my name?

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: I-I did as you asked! Just leave me alone—

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: ...Emma!

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Theo? What happened?

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: I got hit by a carriage, then left behind here.

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: I'm not a Victorian spy, Mrs. Emma... Please, help me... take me to Mr. Culann...

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: A Victorian... spy?

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Ah... it's all happening so fast...

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: It hurts so much...

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: I know the Victorians did bad things. Nobody likes me, nobody listens to me, nobody wants to get close to me.

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: But could you at least... find Mr. Culann... it hurts... it's so cold...

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: When I grow up... I'll find the Victorians and take revenge... for Mr. Niels...

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: (Takes a deep breath)

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Maybe I'd have helped you, Theo, if Niels was the only one who died.

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Mrs... Emma?

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: You know that Niels died in the war, but even more people died without ever seeing the battlefield.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: You Victorians blocked off the supply routes. You still are. So many people starved. Including me, including...

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Including the child Niels left behind... the child inside me.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: He starved to death because of you Victorians.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Find someone else to get Culann for you. They're all good people, unlike me...

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: ...Very good people.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: Emma. How could you do that to him, Emma...?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: What could have changed you so much?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I'm not defending her, Culann, but she wasn't the only one there that day.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: No, she wasn't...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Sorry, shouldn't have said that.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: No, you're absolutely right.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: You wanted to take Theo with you, didn't you? What did you see?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: He was being bullied. And I'm not talkin' squabbles between kids... by adults.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I intervened the first time I saw it. I thought... I thought it wouldn't happen again.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: But it did. A lot.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I had a bad feeling that he didn't belong here, that there was no place for him in Na Saoirsí. But I never thought...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I understand. You should go.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Culann?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I said I understand.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I SAID I UNDERSTAND! NOW GO! GET OUT! LEAVE ME—

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: ...Leave me be for a while. Please.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.
The blacksmith stands silent in the room. All is quiet save for the crackling of the fire.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: Theo, I...
Too many things have passed him by, too many things he could not understand. He no longer has the strength to find out why, to separate cause from effect.
The only thing he knows is that he never achieved anything.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: What kind of hero am I?!
Yeah. What kind of hero are you?
The blacksmith looks around him. There is no one else in the smithy, save the empty eye sockets of the dragon statue, now glaring at him accusingly.

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: What kind of hero are you?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: What... what kind of hero am I?

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: What kind of hero would leave a child to the mercy of abuse and ill-will?

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: What kind of hero would allow food to be smuggled out of the city under his very nose, until there is nothing left. All while doing nothing more than handing out a few shriveled potatoes to his neighbors?

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: What kind of hero would shut himself in his smithy while the city descends into bedlam, all to satisfy his own pathetic vanity by etching his name into a pedestal?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I-It's not out of vanity. All I wanted was to use the title of 'hero' to... to...

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: 'To bring happiness to our countrymen who lost everything in the war,' as you told Nemos?

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: Like now?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: Like... now?

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: The weak you swore to protect are dead and gone.

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: The justice you swore to uphold has fallen into darkness.

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: The people you swore to bring happiness to... Emma and Rory... are they even your people anymore?

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: Or are they the dead, living in the past?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: The dead... living in the past?

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: Your heart still dreams of the future, vain as it is. But them? They are the walking dead, stuck in the past.

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: Who is it you are calling your countrymen? The wretch who spends his days brandishing an antique sword he salvaged from the flames?

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: The smuggler who let an innocent child die because she miscarried her own?

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: 'Townsfolk' who no longer know anything but hate in the face of change?

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: Go on, go out and find someone, anyone. Ask them what their plan for the future is. What do you think the answer will be?
The blacksmith's hammer falls to the ground with a loud crash.
He glares at the dragon's head.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: No, no...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: It's you who's trapping them in the past...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I collected the plates and bowls my people used day to day, lit the fuel they relied on for warmth and light, just to feed you... you...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: You monster.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I don't know about the food. But the metal and the fuel...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: It was me. I fed you those pots and pans, I put the people's livelihoods into your mouth with my own hands, all so that you could grow and grow...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: You've devoured everything in my life, then you devoured Theo himself...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: Theo... Theo...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: It was me, I nurtured the monster that took your life!

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: Soon it will stand in the square on Samhain, spread its wings, and turn everyone in the city into the dead, those who can only live in the past...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: You're right, monster. I'm no hero.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I'm a fraud. A vain, pathetic fraud. Once, I fooled others; now, the only one I'm fooling is myself.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: But they need me.

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: They need you?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: They need a hero to wake them up, to tell them that the war is over, that what really matters is what lies ahead. The future. Tomorrow.

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: And you think you're the one?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I'm the one.
The blacksmith walks away from the forge with resolute steps. He takes the thickest metal chain he can find and walks back to the dragon, its empty eyes still fixated upon him.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: Come with me.

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: Where to?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: To the square.

steps.name: Dragon
steps.text: It's not Samhain yet.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I can wait no more. I will not wait for your ominous prophecies to come true.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: Come with me...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I will dismantle you...

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: And return our lives to the people.
The dragon does not move. In the eyes of the blacksmith, however, he sees the dragon bow its head, perhaps mockingly, perhaps invitingly.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Reed, Nemos, I'm back. Culann's in a real bad place right now. You should go see him.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: How about on your end? What's going on in the city?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: People are still looking for spies... Victorian spies.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Are they off their rockers? Taran or Victorian, we're all human. We gonna keep fighting to the death like this, when the war's already over?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Tell them, Nemos. Tell 'em that Dublinn made 'em go hungry, and was punished by the Red Dragon. The food's now—

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Do not mention the word Dublinn ever again, Brigid. The Leader's orders.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I... only overheard whispers about the food at the victory party. No evidence, no trial.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I don't even know how it got back.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Besides—news about all those missing people hasn't spread at all... How am I supposed to explain it?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: If they can't be reasoned with, we'll do this the hard way.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: When I came back, I told myself I would never be her shadow again.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: But if the true Leader is refusing to show her face and take responsibility, then I must step up, if only to calm the people.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What about Culann? Everyone knows him as a hero. Things would be much simpler if he's willing to help.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: He should still be at his smithy. I'll lead the way.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: As for you, Brigid, you should leave the city as soon as possible.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Well... if we and Culann both fail, then the people will...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I see. They don't much like me here, so I'd just get in the way, is that it?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I'm sorry, Brigid, that's not what I meant, but—

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: But it's true.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Don't worry, I'll try my luck in the Dark Woods. Sixth time's the charm.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Culann!

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Culann...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Is he not in?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: He...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What the...?!
They are both rendered speechless.
The door of the smithy...
No, the entire front wall of the smithy is gone.
The wall, which was supposed to stay up until the statue was finished, is now a pile of rubble. Visible through it is a long trail leading to the square.
Along with drag marks so broad they span almost the entire breadth of the road.
